claim: §4.13's raised-way `wall` cell (l. 9060, R6-02's (P11)) ends '*Rung:* — (defined)', meaning no failure rung. The crossing table's *down before the wall* (l. 2606–2614) gives one: a road deck with fixed ends is 'at generation not built, reported; at an epoch waiting (`raised.waited`)', and a priced deck that cannot come down is 're-routed by the solver's ladder or not built, reported'. The same row's river cell states such a rung ('leave out and report (generated); simpler shape (declared, bent)'). The crossing table governs, so nothing built changes.
required_change: §4.13's raised-way `wall` cell: replace '*Rung:* — (defined)' with '*Rung:* leave out and report (a road deck that cannot come down before a standing trace, at generation; at an epoch it waits, V06 §3.19 (5)); simpler shape (declared, bent: `bend.raised.wall`, `bend.wall.aqueductArch`)'.

claim: CATALOGUE-GAP (C-wall-raised): S5a's pull moves an unpinned deck crossing onto the arterial's ground course. At a stage k >= 2, S5b routes on the stage's picked boundary, and S5a then lays the trace (§4.1's S5 row, base l. 5049: 'S5a L1: the trace with every arterial crossing on ground part 0 as a gate'). S5a Trace (2) (l. 5946-5948) pulls the boundary within a 40 m band toward 'local ridges, slope breaks', pins gates where arterials cross, and 'an arterial crossing the boundary on a raised deck pins no gate there'. Only a raised way's ramps, stairs and feet and an aqueduct's supports are impassable to the pull. So where the picked boundary crosses an S4 or earlier-S5b viaduct's deck within 40 m of a foot on the valley's rim (the high ground the pull seeks), the pulled trace can cross that arterial on its ground course beyond the foot, with no pin and no gate vertex. S5b already counted it out of c (l. 5997). The texts then disagree. §4.1 makes it a gate (N_k + 1 gates). §4.8 Gates says 'exactly N, by construction' (l. 7729). F-WALL's B-CITY bar says 'main gates = N exactly; 0 non-gate crossings', and its ladder would 'divert excess arterials to the nearest gate as lanes' (l. 9203), against 'S4 and S5b arterials are never trimmed' (l. 6055). *beneath*'s '(a way S5a pins no gate for meets the trace as anywhere on ground part 0)' (l. 2627) does not decide which applies. T110-2 (3)'s own c14 fixture ('the arterial on the deck pinning no gate', l. 18555-18561) is this case, with no bar against the pull. The same holds at every epoch stage.
required_change: §4.4 S5a Trace (2), after 'an arterial crossing the boundary on a raised deck pins no gate there,' add: 'and the pull keeps that crossing beneath its deck — that arterial's ground course beyond each foot of the deck, within the search band, impassable to the pull as the deck's ramps, stairs and feet are — so the pulled trace crosses each arterial as the picked boundary did: on ground part 0 at its pin, or under its deck (§2.7's crossing table, *beneath*), and the stage's gates are its pins (`N_k`, §4.4 S5b),'. Second end, at scope: in §13.2 T110-2 (3), after 'the arterial on the deck pinning no gate and S5b's count read on ground part 0', add '— and a variant whose picked boundary crosses that deck within the pull's search band of the valley's rim, the pulled trace crossing it under the deck and never on its ground course beyond the foot, the stage's gates exactly `N_k`, 0 non-gate crossings'.

claim: R6-02 removed the raised gate that carried an S4 viaduct across S3's ring ((P8)) and made a road deck come down before a trace standing when its course is laid (§4.3 *Where it may not go*, l. 5846: 'a deck priced in a route's solve comes down to a ground vertex before the trace … (at S5b the stage's picked boundary counting as standing …)'; §2.7 *down before the wall*, l. 2606–2614, 'S4's or S5b's viaduct'). But S4's gate routes are solved at S3 (5), before any boundary exists ('the gate routes are solved first, the stage-1 boundary is the travel-cost level set over them', l. 5451), with S4's cost function, so CITY and METROPOLIS spans are priced there (§4.3 *The rung gate*, l. 5833; S3 (9) (a), l. 5604–5605). S3 (7) places each gate at 'the first point at which its solved route, walked outward from its plaza, reaches T = t_1' (l. 5564–5565), which may lie on a priced span; S4 'commits the gate routes solved at S3 … without re-solving' (l. 5755), re-solving only a moat's stretch; and the stage-1 trace is committed only at S5a after S4 (§4.1's S5 row, l. 5049). Nothing brings that deck down: the exclusion counts only S5b's picked boundary. Builders differ: the gate kept on the deck (against §4.8 *Gates* 'on ground part 0', *beneath*'s 'No gate on the deck', and S5a *Trace* (2)'s 'an arterial crossing the boundary on a raised deck pins no gate there', which S3 (9) applies — N₁ − 1 gates); the route re-solved at S4; or the S3 trace read as not yet standing and laid after the deck (*beneath*). T110-2 (2) (l. 18549) asserts 'a CITY whose S4 route's best course crosses a valley at S3's gate, its deck down before the trace and its route through the gate on ground part 0', which no mechanism produces. Common at CITY and METROPOLIS on valley sites, and at every regeneration that re-lays S4's viaducts (W3·C1).
required_change: §4.2 S3 (7), after 'on the boundary by construction; the gate keeps the pick's identity, ordinal, bearing and route.' add: 'A route whose first point at `T = t_1` lies on a raised stretch of its solved course (a viaduct (5)'s solve priced, §4.3) is re-solved whole as (5) solves it, every deck edge across the stage-1 boundary excluded (the boundary counting as standing, §4.3 *Where it may not go*; §2.7's crossing table, *down before the wall*), and its gate is the re-solved route's first point at `T = t_1`, on ground part 0; `T` and the boundary keep (5)'s routes and are not re-derived; a route the re-solve cannot serve takes F-ROUTE's ladder (§5.2), reported.' §4.3 *Where it may not go* (l. 5846): '(at S5b the stage's picked boundary counting as standing;' → '(at S3 (7) the stage-1 boundary, from S3 (9) on its trace, and at S5b the stage's picked boundary counting as standing;'. END at model: §2.7 *down before the wall* (l. 2607) '— at S5b the stage's picked boundary counting as standing;' → '— at S3 (7) the stage-1 boundary, from S3 (9) on its trace, and at S5b the stage's picked boundary counting as standing;'.

claim: (P9) (§4.11 `wallToWay`, l. 8282) re-routes the ring road 'in the dry run … to cross under the nearest span §4.3's crossing rule admits', and in the same commit 'V04 lays again the arch vault of a `vault` span the old wall stood over'. The crossing rule bars a `vault` span's under-deck strip but reads 'a `vault` span under a wall … `open`' (way-and-channel table lead, l. 2576–2578), and *beneath* reads it `open` 'while that band or strip lies there' (l. 2640–2645). In `wallToWay`'s dry run the band and strips still lie there; they go only with the op (l. 8278–8281). Under *beneath* the old line itself crosses an aqueduct's deck line under a span (l. 2618–2620), which may be a `vault` span. One builder reads the pre-op state: the span `open`, the crossing admitted, the ring road kept on the old line under it — then V04's reconcile in the `wallToWay` commit (V04 l. 328, 867) lays the arch vault's chamber at grade across the new road, failing T110-2 (8)'s and T-V6-47's '0 way corridors over … a `vault` span's strip' (T110-2's lead counts '`vault` spans no wall stands over'). Another reads the post-op state and re-routes the road under another span. H-AQUA's aqueduct carries `vault` spans (T-V6-47 breaches one), so T-V6-47's `wallToWay` runs reach the case.
required_change: §4.11 `wallToWay` (l. 8282): 'to cross under the nearest span §4.3's crossing rule admits' → 'to cross under the nearest span §4.3's crossing rule admits, each `vault` span the old wall stood over read `vault` (no band or strip lies there once the op commits; §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*)'. END at model: the way-and-channel table's row (c) outcome (l. 2584) 'the same, the old line being where it is laid' → 'the same, the old line being where it is laid and a `vault` span the old wall stood over read `vault`'. END at scope: §13.2 T110-2 (8) adds 'and the same on a fixture whose old line passed under a `vault` span of a standing aqueduct — the ring road re-routed under another span, the arch vault laid again with no way corridor over its strip'.

claim: §4.11 *Other crossings* (l. 8302–8312): the run of a wall a carve crosses is re-traced by S7's operator; 'Every way the re-traced run's new strips … will meet, other than a kept way through a gate of the run …, takes the `cut` fate', and 'A locked or pinned way, wall or finer entity, or a reservation, inside `S` or inside a new strip returns to the dry run as an F-EDIT conflict'. §7.3 (b) 3 (l. 11027–11029) says the same for S1's water operator (a moved river). A raised way's supports, ramps, stairs, feet and `vault`-span strips are 'a reservation on ground part 0' (§2.7's support step (6), l. 2565–2567), and a raised way is a way. Before round 6 the new strips stopped at the under-deck strip's edges, so they held none of these; round 6 runs the strips (and the band, through a road deck's support) on beneath the deck (*beneath*; (M1): 'a support may stand' in the setback and glacis). Now §4.11 refuses the carve (or cuts the raised way) where §7.3's S7 operator meets the raised way 'by §2.7's crossing table (*beneath*) — nothing of the raised way re-derived' (l. 10927), *beneath* lays the strips 'as anywhere', and §7.1's lock row says a lock never refuses 'a carve or a wall stretch passing beneath a locked or pinned raised way's deck'. The crossing table has no row for this event (W2 names 'a hand `drawWall`, a moved trace vertex or a re-anchored stretch'), and *beneath*'s bent group does not list it. Two outcomes for one case (R6-01: MAJOR however rare).
required_change: §4.11 *Other crossings* (l. 8307–8312): 'other than a kept way through a gate of the run (whose corridor ends each strip, §4.8),' → 'other than a kept way through a gate of the run (whose corridor ends each strip, §4.8) and a raised way, whose deck passes over the run,'; and after 'returns to the dry run as an F-EDIT conflict (lock > drawn geometry; Re-derive from S3 offered for a reservation, §5.2), as for S1's water operator.' add 'A standing raised way — locked, pinned or neither — and its reservation are no conflict: the re-traced run meets it by §2.7's crossing table (*beneath*, row W2), bent locally where *beneath* says, each bend a fate, nothing of the raised way changed (§7.1's lock row).' END at determinism: §7.3 (b) 3 (l. 11027–11029) 'or a reservation there — returns to the dry run (§7.1's outcome table)' → 'or a reservation there (never a standing raised way or its reservation, which a re-traced run meets by §2.7's crossing table, *beneath*) — returns to the dry run (§7.1's outcome table)'. END at model: the crossing table's W2 event cell (l. 2699) 'a hand `drawWall`, a moved trace vertex or a re-anchored stretch' → 'a hand `drawWall`, a moved trace vertex, a re-anchored stretch, or a run a carve or a moved river re-traces (§4.11 *Other crossings*; §7.3 (b) 3)'; *beneath*'s bent-group list (l. 2628–2629) adds 'a run a carve or a moved river re-traces'. END at scope: T110-2 (5) adds 'a hand carve of a canal across a ring beneath which a standing locked aqueduct passes, the re-traced run's strips meeting its supports: no F-EDIT conflict, the run *beneath*, the aqueduct unchanged'.

claim: The way-and-channel table's row (e) (l. 2586) and T110-2 (3) (l. 18564–18565) say a moat stopped at an under-deck strip leaves 'the wall's outer strip closed across the under-deck strip as on a dry stretch (§4.7 S10 (0))'. S10 (0) (l. 6871–6874) types `ditch` 'along a moat's dry stretches, §4.2 S3 (10)' — S3 (10)'s water-level stretches only — and §4.8 *Wall strips* (l. 7699–7701) bounds the outer strip 'by the moat's inner bank' wherever 'a moat runs along the wall', naming no stopped gap. A builder of S7 and S10 (0) reading the cited homes types that gap `glacis`; row (e) says dry-stretch (`ditch`). The home states the outcome; the sections it cites omit it.
required_change: §4.7 S10 (0) (l. 6873–6874): 'and along a moat's dry stretches, §4.2 S3 (10))' → 'and along a moat's dry stretches, §4.2 S3 (10), and across an under-deck strip where a moat is stopped, §2.7's way-and-channel table, row (e))'; §4.8 *Wall strips* (l. 7700–7701): '— or, where a moat runs along the wall, by the moat's inner bank, the strip then being the band's half plus the berm.' → '— or, where a moat runs along the wall, by the moat's inner bank, the strip then being the band's half plus the berm; across an under-deck strip where the moat is stopped (§2.7's way-and-channel table, row (e)) by the glacis line, as on a dry stretch.'
